meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
You called this meeting, Hale, so I'll let you start. I have a call at 4:40, and I'd like to know who decided on the zero, and whether anyone spoke to Owen before it went in.
I'm waiting, Hale. The zero went in before anyone called me, so start there.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still want Owen's zero withdrawn, an explanation of who decided on it and whether Owen was heard first, and an assurance that nothing goes on his record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Opening position, she agreed to nothing and still wants the zero withdrawn, an account of who decided it, and Owen's record kept clean.
What moved her: Nothing, because Hale offered only a polite greeting and no ownership or document.
What cost ground: Nothing, though answering her direct question about the zero with a pleasantry let her press harder.
Try next time: When she asks who decided on the zero and whether Owen was heard, own in one sentence that the mark went in before anyone called home, then show her a dated document from Owen's own work.
